look_here_first: Start at a stem node: opposite, pinnately compound leaves with serrate leaflets, then a broad terminal cluster of small flowers. Confirm the American elderberry concept from provenance; flower color and leaflet count alone do not separate it from European Sambucus nigra.

best_field_traits: Opposite compound leaves, usually with 5–11 serrate leaflets; robust shoots can have twice-compound leaves.
Broad terminal cymose panicle, typically with five primary rays.
Small radially symmetric, usually five-part flowers; UT Austin local treatment also allows four-part flowers.
morphology_keys.habit: Many-stemmed deciduous shrub or small tree; local flowering specimens about 1.5–4+ m tall.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite and decussate, odd-pinnately compound; leaflet margins serrate.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Terminal, flat-topped to domed panicle of cymes, 75–384 mm across in the UT Austin local treatment; usually five primary rays.
morphology_keys.flower: Flowers 5–6.3 mm across in the local treatment; shallow rotate corolla with 4–5 lobes and stamens; ovary described there as half-inferior.
morphology_keys.fruit: Glossy black, not waxy, drupes about 4.3–5.2 × 5–6.2 mm, with 3–5 hard pyrenes.
morphology_keys.lookalike_separators: Viburnum: simple opposite leaves and usually one stone, versus compound elder leaves and multiple pyrenes. Sambucus nigra s.s.: overlapping heads, dark fruit, and leaflet counts; require documented origin or voucher, not a photo-only confident key. S. cerulea: often waxy blue fruit, but wax can rub off.

project_inclusion.range_basis: POWO includes Texas in native distribution at state scale. Existing review has not certified at least three project target-zone counties; preserve UNRESOLVED.
